scope.origin: User-pinned 2026-09-14: happiness and harmony in the spirit of blume.codes, a literal road map, playful, a car on the road. Same day the user chose system emojis for every illustrated object that has one (over bundled Twemoji or Noto, accepting per-platform differences), varied houses, flowers and trees, and a car the visitor picks at the start. The landscape stays its own layer so painted art can replace it later.

display-finish.purpose: Finish headline, the largest type on the page.

title.purpose: Signpost board heading; 22px at 760px and below. Stone numerals use the display face at 19px (17px narrow).

wordmark.purpose: roadmap-live lowercase in the top bar; 22px narrow.

button.purpose: Primary command pill label (15px copy chip, 14px narrow); answer pills and links use 600 at 16px.

motion.name: ease-ui
motion.purpose: Pill lift 220ms, picker lift 180ms, car hop 440ms, bubble pop 380ms, sign rise 520ms.

motion.name: color-fade
motion.purpose: Background and color changes on tabs, command rows, answer pills and picker buttons; stone turns red over 400ms.

motion.name: cloud-drift
motion.value: translateX(-36px to 36px), 46s / 54s / 62s / 70s, ease-in-out, infinite alternate, staggered delays

motion.name: hero-roll-in
motion.value: 300ms delay; translate(650 1010) scale(1.3) to translate(650 812) scale(1) over 1900ms, cubic ease-out, bob sin(k*26)*(1-k)*1.5
motion.purpose: The hero car arrives at the start line once.

motion.name: car-hop
motion.value: hero car emoji scale(-1, 1) translateY(0 to -28px to 0), 440ms ease-ui, via Web Animations; skipped under reduced motion and on restore

motion.name: scroll-car
motion.value: probe at 55% viewport height; hold zone ±130px (±70px at 760px and below) around each stop; ease 16% of remaining distance per frame, snap below 0.6px; reached within 30px

motion.name: car-pose
motion.value: facing flips when the path's normalized dx passes ±0.25 (hysteresis); tilt = min(38deg, atan2(|dy|, |dx|)) signed by dy, times facing; bob sin(rolled/9)*1.2px with rolled += |step|*0.5; transform translate rotate(facing*tilt) scaleX(-facing)
motion.purpose: The emoji car looks left by default; it faces its direction of travel, noses along the slope and bobs gently.

motion.name: sign-arrival
motion.value: unreached signs translateY(10px); rise over 520ms ease-ui on reach
motion.purpose: Signs settle as the car arrives.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.value: clouds, pops and car hop off; pill, sign, stone and answer transitions off; signs do not sink; hero car stays at the start line; road car parks at the last stop within 60px of the probe, or at the flag

motion.name: no-js
motion.value: straight 42px tar strip centered (26px at the right edge narrow); car and flag hidden; stones red; picker shows the default car pressed

breakpoints.name: wide
breakpoints.purpose: Demo window takes gutter margins; flora moves inward and shrinks (72px and 40px).

breakpoints.name: medium
breakpoints.purpose: Lane 96px; signs stretch to their full column.

breakpoints.name: narrow
breakpoints.purpose: Gutter 16px; hero min-height 960px; road in a 44px edge lane opposite each sign; scenery below signs in 168px bands with two props (52px, 48px); posts, dots, flora, finish scene hidden; picker 36px buttons with the label on its own line; thinner road strokes; road car and flag 46px; desktop sun swapped for a low rising sun, plus a mobile-only tree and tulip.

layers: art (z -3, drawn ground plus emoji text, swappable for a painted raster)

emoji.variety: each scene: one anchor of 88px or more, mixed tree kinds, varied house and flower kinds, a small animal or ground detail at 34 to 60px; repeats only as a deliberate cluster
mobileOnly: rising sun ☀️ at 640,622 size 76 over a 110 glow
desktopOnly: sun ☀️ at 1190,296 size 124 over a 190 glow

inkOutline.optOut: stroke="none" on highlights and the contact shadow

road.path: cubic segments with vertical handles (half the vertical distance) through each lane point; desktop points swing min(lane*0.3, 44)px toward the sign side; narrow points run straight from sign top-14 to bottom+14

hedges.placement: along two of every three field edges; clumps of 3 to 8; font-size 2.4 x r, r 8-16 (5-10 narrow); spacing 1.9 x r; gaps 70-290px (40-130px narrow); vertical jitter ±4px; seeded deterministically
hedges.shadow: hedgerow drop shadow on the group

car.hero: 🚗 by default, 126 frame units, mirrored with scale(-1 1) to face right, on a contact ellipse at the start line
car.road: same emoji as the hero, 64px in a 72px box (46px in 54px narrow), pose per motion.car-pose
car.picker: choice stored in localStorage key rl-car and restored only if it matches a picker button

finish.flag: 🏁 emoji at the road end, offset 40px right (58px left narrow)

narrative.overview:
The roadmap is a real road through a sunny landscape. A small car, the one the visitor picked, waits at the start line under a deep blue sky, and as the visitor scrolls it drives down a winding slate road through meadow fields, pausing beside wooden signposts that each explain one step of the product. The origin is pinned by the user: happiness and harmony in the spirit of blume.codes, a literal road map, playful. On 2026-09-14 the user chose system emojis for every illustrated object that has one, accepting that they look different on each platform; the landscape stays its own layer so painted art can replace it later.

The world is daylight only. Sky blue melts to a warm cream ground; everything below the horizon is layered greens, each field a distinct soft tint. The ground (sky, hills, fields, road, verge, start line) is drawn in SVG; what stands on it (trees, houses, animals, flowers, clouds, sun, the car, the flag) is a color emoji, varied in kind and size, casting a soft green shadow. Content never sits in boxes: it hangs as paper notices pinned under wooden boards on posts. Shapes are rounded, shadows are diffuse and tinted by what they fall on. Density is low and paced by the road: one stop, one idea, a lot of meadow in between.

The page refuses the dark developer-tool look and the kanban screenshot hero. The product's real page appears once, in a paper window rising out of the meadow, quiet and gray, so the landscape carries the feeling and the window carries the proof.
keyCharacteristics: Full-bleed illustrated hero: drawn sky gradient, hills and a road winding to the horizon, dressed with emoji sun, clouds, trees, houses, animals and flowers; the picked car at a checkered start line.
A "Pick your car" row of round emoji toggles under the hero command; the choice drives the whole page and is remembered.
One road down the page, generated from the layout, with the car mapped to scroll, facing its direction of travel and held beside each sign.
Wooden signpost boards with numbered milestone stones, paper notices with two pin dots, a post into the grass.
Young Serif for display and boards, Onest for sentences, system mono only for commands, the system emoji stack for everything illustrated.
Sunflower yellow only where a human is needed; cherry red for the way forward.
Grain texture multiplied over sky, meadow and wood.

rules.name: The Sunflower Rule
rules.body: In the interface layer, sunflower yellow fills only what needs a human: attention tags and the agent's open question. When the visitor answers, the bubble returns to paper and the question tag turns gray. The illustration may grow sunflower emojis; no button, board, link or heading may be yellow.

rules.name: The Way Forward Red Rule
rules.body: Cherry red belongs to what moves you forward: the primary command pill and a reached stone. It is never a warning and never a text color. The car's own color comes from the emoji the visitor picked, not from a token.

rules.name: The Daylight Rule
rules.body: No dark mode and no dark section. Light text appears only on the sky, on cherry red (pill, reached stone) and on wood boards; everywhere else text is ink on paper, cream or meadow.

rules.name: The Signpost Voice Rule
rules.body: Young Serif speaks only at display sizes, on boards, on stones and in the wordmark. Every sentence is Onest; emphasis is 600, never italic, never a third weight.

rules.name: The Copyable Mono Rule
rules.body: Mono appears only for a command or a file name. If it is not something the visitor would type or open, it is not mono.

rules.name: The Road Owns the Middle Rule
rules.body: On wide screens the road runs down the center lane and signs never cross it; on narrow screens the road takes the edge and signs take the rest. Generated fields and hedgerows keep 24px clear of every sign.

rules.name: The Tinted Shadow Rule
rules.body: Shadows take the color of what lies beneath: green over meadow, brown under wood, deep red under the red pill, blue on the sky. No neutral gray outer shadows and no hard offset drop shadows; the only zero-blur edges are inset: the pill bevel (inset 0 -3px 0) and the answer pill ring.

rules.name: The Grounded Prop Rule
rules.body: Below the hero, nothing floats in the meadow: an emoji prop casts its green drop shadow downward, a drawn object stands on a flat ellipse.

rules.name: The No Hard Corner Rule
rules.body: The smallest interface corner is 3px. The only square interface edge is where paper meets wood.

rules.name: The Nothing Faster Than the Car Rule
rules.body: Motion is gentle ease-out (cubic-bezier(0.2, 0.8, 0.2, 1) for interface, 160 to 520ms). Clouds drift for tens of seconds; the car is the fastest thing on the page, and only moves when the visitor scrolls, picks a car, or first arrives.

rules.name: The Swappable Landscape Rule
rules.body: Art, grain, car and copy are separate layers sharing one frame. Replacing the landscape means replacing one layer and keeping the start line at x 650, y 812 of 1440 by 900.

rules.name: The System Emoji Rule
rules.body: If an object has an emoji, it is that emoji in the system emoji stack. Variety comes from choosing a different emoji, never from tinting, outlining or redrawing one. Draw in SVG only the ground and what no emoji fits.

rules.name: The Mixed Meadow Rule
rules.body: Every scene mixes kinds and sizes: one anchor of 88px or more (a house or a big tree), smaller trees, and ground-level flowers, animals or mushrooms of 34 to 60px. Houses and flowers vary in kind across the page; a repeated emoji in one scene is a deliberate cluster (the three sunflowers at the attention stop), not filler.

dos: Do hang content as a paper notice under a wooden board on a post, numbered with a milestone stone.
Do use a system emoji for every tree, house, animal, flower, cloud, sun, car and flag, in the Apple Color Emoji, Segoe UI Emoji, Noto Color Emoji stack.
Do vary props within a scene: one 88px-plus anchor, mixed tree kinds, different house kinds, several flower kinds, a small animal or ground detail.
Do give every emoji prop below the hero the drop shadow 0 8px 5px rgb(40 64 20 / 0.22), and stand drawn objects on a contact ellipse.
Do tint shadows by what they fall on: green rgb(40 72 28) over meadow, rgb(60 40 20) under wood, rgb(110 30 12) under the red pill, rgb(10 40 90) on the sky.
Do keep the hero art and car layers on the 1440 by 900 frame with xMidYMax slice and the start line at x 650, y 812.
Do let the picked car follow the visitor everywhere a car appears, and mirror it with scaleX so it faces its direction of travel.
Do keep sunflower yellow for attention tags and the agent's open question, and return them to calm once answered.
Do park the car at each stop under reduced motion and draw a plain road without JavaScript.
donts: Don't use sunflower yellow on buttons, boards, links, headings or any interface element that does not need a human.
Don't use red for errors, warnings or text; red is the way forward.
Don't add a dark section or a dark mode, or put light text on anything but sky, cherry red or wood.
Don't put content in bordered boxes or cards; use signs, notices, bubbles or the window.
Don't set sentences in Young Serif or anything except commands and file names in mono.
Don't draw an SVG symbol, bundle an emoji font, or recolor an emoji for an object that has one.
Don't rotate the car to the road tangent or tilt it past 38 degrees; it drives side-on.
Don't use corners below 3px, neutral gray shadows, or hard offset drop shadows.
Don't let anything move faster than the car or move without the visitor's input, except the drifting clouds, the one-time hero roll-in and the picker hop.
